title: Mouse Without Borders mouse rubberbanding with 1000hz/polling rate for mouse and keyboards

status.label: High-rate mouse coalescing design ready
status.detail: Packet rate scales sharply with polling rate and every move is forwarded individually.

next_action.label: Review coalescing investigation
next_action.reason: Bound redundant movement while preserving discrete input ordering.

judgment.rationale: Reproduction and packet measurements align with the per-event send/receive path. A bounded move-only coalescing design is plausible, gated by current diagnostics.
evidence: Packet rate rises from about 400/s at 125 Hz to about 3000/s at 1000 Hz.
Repeated clicking also reproduces on wired LAN.
Each event is sent and applied individually.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a move-event coalescing investigation and collect a current high-rate trace.

fix_assessment.rationale: The hot path is identifiable, but the safe boundary must preserve button, wheel, drag, and machine-switch ordering.

proposed_fixes.title: Bound high-frequency remote mouse movement
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Forwarding every high-rate move independently creates queueing and stale movement around discrete transitions.
plan: Measure movement send, receive, and application rates.
Retain only the newest pending move per peer while a send is in flight.
Flush before button, wheel, drag, destination, or machine-switch transitions.
Add sampled diagnostics and ordering tests.
verification: Test 125, 500, and 1000 Hz on wired and wireless networks.
Confirm smooth movement, no repeated clicks, and preserved discrete input.

confidence.rationale: Measurements align with the per-event path, but current traces must distinguish transport from receiver scheduling.

issue_context.summary: Mouse Without Borders rubber-bands at 1000 Hz, with packet rate scaling steeply and repeated clicks also reported on wired LAN.
known_information: About 3000 packets/s were measured at 1000 Hz.
The implementation forwards and applies every event.
inferences: Application-side overhead is plausible and not limited to Wi-Fi.
Movement-only coalescing could help, but discrete ordering is safety-critical.
issue_context.analysis: The useful correction is a bounded movement path, not generic throttling.
initial_investigation: Event.MouseEvent calls Common.SkSend for each event.
No movement-specific coalescing boundary is visible.

information_gaps.information: Current version, mouse/polling rate, topology, exact symptom, and failure-time archive.
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes transport overload, receiver scheduling, and input injection.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce on current stable, report the environment, then comment /bugreport immediately.

actions.label: Approve bounded mouse-move coalescing investigation
actions.design_summary: Coalesce only redundant movement and flush before every discrete transition.

comment.body:
The packet measurements and wired-LAN reproduction are useful. Please provide:

1. The current PowerToys version, mouse model, polling rate, and network topology.
2. Whether the failure is rubber-banding, repeated clicks, or both.
3. A fresh diagnostic archive by commenting `/bugreport` immediately after reproducing.

This will distinguish transport queueing from receiver or input-injection behavior.

author: Shineblind
